messages:
Maya: Heads up — seeing exporter queue blowups on gateway during bursty deploys. Agent memory spikes, then gateway backs up and we start dropping spans. Curious trade-offs: agent-local caps + spill vs central gateway throttling?
Ethan: Can you paste a quick repro or logs?
Maya: Logs: https://our-logs/xyz — basically exporter blocked for ~45s, agent buffer grew to ~120MB and OOM-killed a pod.
Priya: Ouch. For spans I think TTL-based eviction + size caps per-signal is ok. If queue > threshold, drop least-important spans (low-sampled or >Nms latency).
Jon: Disk spill helps but adds IO and complexity. We could prefer sampled root spans and drop internals when under pressure.
infra-bot: Note: creating metric agent_exporter_queue_bytes for alerting (auto-rule).
Priya: We already tag spans with qos_priority and sampling_reason. Use those to score for eviction. Also consider per-tenant token-bucket to limit exporter throughput instead of hard drops.
Ethan: Config-wise: agent-per-signal pipelines let us enforce local caps nearer to source, but increase memory duplication. Gateway-centralized gives global batching gains and smarter retention decisions.
Maya: Right — proposal: keep lightweight agent pipelines with small ring buffers and immediate drop policy; gateway owns long-term batching, intelligent retention and reordering. Need precise semantics for "spill to gateway" and TTL ordering.
Jon: Hybrid idea: agent stores metadata and a compact trace index, forwards full spans async when network unconstrained. Gateway requests full payloads on demand or retrieves from agent store.
Priya: That avoids double-write for every burst. But we need retention guarantees and expired-index garbage collection. Add eviction metric to console.
Maya: UX side: console should show per-tenant queue depth, per-signal retention eviction rate, and a timeline of spill events. Rollout flag: "adaptive-spill" with canary on 10% tenants.
Ethan: I'll prototype a token-bucket limiter + retention eviction test harness. Patch will include new config block: 
```
exporter:
  queue_max_bytes: 50MB
  spill_to_disk: true
  retention_ttl: 30s
  eviction_policy: qos_score
```
Priya: Tests should cover: 1) spill-then-drop, 2) priority-based eviction, 3) gateway fallback when agent unreachable.
sre-oncall: If this impacts production, fallback plan: route traces to alternate exporter region and enable emergency-drop-mode to preserve running services.
Jon: We should also add a small in-proc sampling amplifier so critical spans get through even during drops.
Maya: Good call. Also add a feature flag per-deployment for hybrid-indexing approach. I'll sketch a spec and upload to the design doc.
Ethan: I'll send a draft PR for the limiter and a load test job targeting the exporter path tomorrow.
Priya: I'll wire the console metrics and a small dashboard mock for the rollout.
Maya: Thanks all. Sync tomorrow 10am to review PR + dashboard.
Jon: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Reminder: scheduled infra window at 02:00 UTC tonight — may affect canary runs.
sre-oncall: noted, will coordinate.
